discovery_tool_ladder.consensus: Invoked 2026-08-27 — query 'APOE epsilon allele defining SNPs rs429358 rs7412 chromosome 19 genomic coordinates GRCh37'; 20 papers returned. No paper asserts a genomic coordinate (literature reports APOE variants by codon/coding position, not by build coordinate). It did surface the two records now cited as the rsID-to-coding-position anchor. The returned result set is retained, reduced to citation identity, at raw/consensus-search-apoe-grch37-derived.json; Consensus returns through an MCP tool rather than an HTTP endpoint, so no verbatim wire payload exists to keep.

independence_note: Ensembl Variation imports rsID-to-coordinate mappings from dbSNP, so the Ensembl and dbSNP records share an upstream assertion and do NOT by themselves satisfy the two-agreeing-source rule. The independent mapping source is VariantValidator, which was given only the APOE coding HGVS and no rsID, and which projects the variant onto GRCh37 through RefSeq/UTA transcript alignments rather than through the dbSNP rsID record. The UCSC hg19 reference bases are an additional assembly-level control: they are necessary-but-not-sufficient for the positive claim, and decisive for excluding the rejected coordinates. For the three APOE-region neighbours (rs405509, rs440446, rs769449) the position is fully independent only in part, and that is disclosed rather than papered over: they are non-coding, so there is no coding HGVS to project and the rsID-to-locus assertion has a single upstream lineage (dbSNP, mirrored by Ensembl). What IS independent is the cross-build correspondence and the reference base: VariantValidator, given the genomic HGVS, validates the GRCh37 REF and returns GRCh38 19:44905579 / 19:44905910 / 19:44906745, which match dbSNP's chrpos for rs405509 / rs440446 / rs769449 respectively -- and that is what establishes the mispairing, since the fixture had rs440446 on rs405509's GRCh38 coordinate. These three rows carry no analytic weight: no module reads them, and they exist as APOE-region context in a vendor fixture.
sanitization: None required. Every retained payload is a public reference-database, variant-mapping, or bibliographic record. No genotype, sample, personal, or credentialed data is present, and no payload was edited.
